chunks: And Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a woman who comes performing tamattu‘, then menstruates before she performs tawaf of the House, until she goes out to Arafat. He said: "It becomes a separate hajj (hajj ifrad), and she must offer the blood of her sacrifice."

key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the Ka'bah, the Sacred House
key_terms.حَجَّةً مُفْرَدَةً: Hajj al-Ifrad, a standalone form of hajj
key_terms.دَمُ أُضْحِيَّتِهَا: the blood of her sacrificial animal, meaning the required sacrifice
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the major station of hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman performing tamattu‘ menstruates before tawaf and goes to Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu‘ who menstruates before completing tawaf and must leave for Arafat. The Imam عليه السلام rules that her rite becomes Hajj al-Ifrad, and she remains liable for the sacrificial offering.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2760 - Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (as) about a woman performing tamattu‘ who begins menstruating before she can perform tawaf of the Kaaba and then proceeds to Arafat.
Imam (as) said: "Her Hajj becomes an ifrad (Hajj alone), and she is required to offer the sacrifice of her hady (sacrificial animal)."
